nodes.label: Personal Data Redaction
nodes.rationale: Bug reporters must manually redact messages, names, links, and other personal information before submitting error details.

nodes.label: Existing Issue Search
nodes.rationale: Contributors should search and support an existing request before creating a duplicate feature request.

nodes.label: Development Version Release Guard
nodes.rationale: Development-version artifacts may be built only by explicit request and must never be released.

nodes.label: Credential-Free Pull Request Execution
nodes.rationale: Untrusted pull-request code is executed without privileged credentials, while cache credentials are restricted to read-only access.

nodes.label: Lint Type Unit and Rust Quality Gate
nodes.norm_label: lint type unit and rust quality gate

nodes.label: Trusted-Code Cache Publication
nodes.rationale: Only trusted main-branch code may populate the writable dependency cache consumed read-only by pull-request checks.

nodes.label: Scoped Graphify Query Workflow
nodes.rationale: Scoped query, path, explain, and wiki navigation should be used before broad report or raw source browsing to reduce irrelevant context.

nodes.label: No Project-Level Monetary Donations
nodes.rationale: Open Grind has no governance entity that can accept money on the project's behalf; donations go to individual contributors instead.

nodes.label: Analytics Documentation Omission
nodes.rationale: Detailed analytics documentation is intentionally deprioritized because behavioral tracking conflicts with Open Grind's values.

nodes.label: Session ID Cache
nodes.rationale: Session IDs should be cached until expiry or invalidation to avoid unnecessary sign-in calls and rate limits.

nodes.label: Privacy by Default
nodes.rationale: Open Grind is positioned to collect no analytics or user data and to include no trackers.

nodes.label: Security as Foundation
nodes.rationale: Human review, audits, supply-chain security, and end-to-end testing are presented as foundational product practices.

nodes.label: Partial Platform Support Qualification
nodes.rationale: iOS, Windows, and Linux are described as technically supported but not yet tested or available as stable builds.

nodes.label: Permissive Software Grant
nodes.rationale: Recipients may use, copy, modify, merge, publish, distribute, sublicense, and sell the software provided the notice is retained.

nodes.label: Warranty and Liability Disclaimer
nodes.rationale: The software is supplied as-is without warranties, and authors or copyright holders disclaim liability.
